title: Hosted Interaction Suite PRD and Cutover Runbook (Composable Chat, Generation, Embedding, Rerank)
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-level PRD for a bundled hosted API surface that exposes composable chat, text generation (completions), embeddings, and rerank endpoints as a cohesive product. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, and a cutover/runbook for launch. Focus is on developer ergonomics, clear behavioral contracts, measurable SLOs, and safe rollout mechanics. Target customers: PLG developers and platform teams who need predictable latency, cost levers, and fallbacks across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.
goals:
- Provide a single, discoverable product bundle (Hosted Interaction Suite) covering chat, generation, embeddings, and rerank with consistent auth, quota, and telemetry.
- Define API contracts and failure/degenerate behavior for each endpoint so downstream integration is predictable.
- Ship a staged rollout with canary traffic, observability dashboards, and automated rollback criteria.
- Ensure cost/latency knobs (batching, model variant routing, quantization profile) are exposed as recommendations in console and SDKs.
- Avoid regressions in quality vs. existing hosted lanes (embedding similarity, generation F1/ROUGE proxies, chat coherence).
out_of_scope:
- On-prem/air-gapped installer changes (Private will consume same API surface but separate ticket handles infra packaging).
- Deep model architecture changes or re-training.
- SDK language expansions beyond Node/Python for MVP.
- Enterprise contract/legal negotiation — handled by Sales/Early Access separate process.
api_contract_summary:
Chat:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/chat.generate
- Behavior: incremental streaming + final JSON envelope for structured outputs. Must support function/tool calling and message-level role metadata.
Completions/Generation:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate
- Behavior: deterministic options (seed/temperature), token limits, stop sequences. Streaming optional.
Embeddings:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings
- Behavior: returns fixed-length float vectors per input item, batch support, truncation policy documented.
Rerank:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/rerank
- Behavior: takes N candidates + query, returns ranked list with scores and optional rationale; stable sorting on ties.
Common: auth bearer token, per-token billing metadata header, plain JSON contract with versioned schema v1.0, backward-compatible additive changes only for v1.x line.
requirements:
1) Behavioral: Clearly documented deterministic fallback behaviors when a model variant is unavailable (e.g., fallback chain: high-quality spend -> medium-cost quantized -> regional fallback).
2) Latency/Performance: Provide SLOs (p95) per endpoint for typical request shapes (see acceptance_criteria).
3) Observability: Out-of-the-box dashboards per route: token-cost, p50/p95 latency, error-rate, reject-rate, successful-stream-rate.
4) Billing/Quota: Integrate with existing billing meter for per-token and per-embedding accounting, plus quota enforcement hooks for free/paid tiers.
5) Security: Token auth, audit-logging for private deployments, and a security review checklist before GA.
6) SDK: Node + Python minimal helpers for streaming and pagination; examples for batching embeddings and rerank canonicalization.
7) Release controls: Canary targeting by org/id, progressive rollout percentages, automatic circuit breaker on capacity signals.
8) Acceptance testing harness: deterministic prompt sets for quality regression checks, embedding similarity test corpus, and rerank relevance dataset.
9) Docs and examples: Quickstarts for chat and similarity search, migration guide for existing hosted endpoints.
10) Rollback safety: Automatic traffic switch to previous stable model variant and feature-flag for emergency disable at route level.
acceptance_criteria:
- API contract implemented and validated by contract tests (postman/newman or equivalent).
- Latency SLOs met in staging under realistic traffic patterns: chat p95 <= 350ms for short-turn (<=128 tokens) on hosted lane; generation p95 <= 450ms for 256-token requests; embeddings p95 <= 120ms for batch size 16.
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx errors across all endpoints during a 72h soak in canary.
- Quality regression gates: embedding average cosine similarity to golden pairs within +/-1.5% of baseline median; generation fluency/regression score (BLEU/ROUGE proxy on curated prompts) no worse than -3 points vs baseline.
- SDKs publish usage examples and at least one integration example (search + rerank) in GH repo with passing CI.
- Observability: pre-populated dashboards and alert rules available in Console. Alerts include: error_rate>0.5% over 5m, p95 latency > 2x expected baseline for 5m, queue-depth/backpressure signals > threshold.
- Billing: per-token/per-embedding invoicing events emitted in prod audit log and verified in sample customer invoice.
- Security: security review completed and issues remediated (critical/major fixed or TODO tracked).
- Docs: public PRD-style docs + migration guide in docs site published and linked from Console onboarding.
- Rollout automation: runbook automated to flip 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each step. Manual gate for last 50->100.
- GA readiness: Customer-facing feature checklist signed off by PM, Eng, Design, and Solutions Engineering leads.
cutover_runbook:
Pre-cutover (to run 48-24h before):
- Confirm staging soak metrics green for 72h; check SLO dashboards.
- Finalize release candidate model pins and compatibility matrix; tag artifacts in registry.
- Notify beta customers and internal stakeholders with expected windows.
- Run migration dry-run for token/quota enforcement in staging.
Canary (day 0):
- Launch step 1: route 5% of traffic from a small org slice (internal test orgs + 5 partner orgs). Monitor 15m windows after warmup.
- Health checks: p95 latency, 5xx rate, token billing events, and quality gates on sample prompts.
- If green, escalate to 25% after 1 hour.
Progressive rollout: 25% -> 50% following 2h stable windows and manual sign-off for 50->100.
Automated rollback triggers:
- sustained 5xx > 0.8% for 10m
- p95 latency breach > 2x for 10m
- Quality gate failure on scheduled evals (nightly regression jobs)
Rollback actions:
- Trigger automated traffic switch to previous stable variant, notify on-call, open incident ticket, and block further rollouts.
Post-cutover:
- Verify billing events and quota enforcement for sampled customers.
- Run 24h quality-runbook for embeddings/regression checks; escalate if regressions detected.
- Collect customer feedback for first 2 weeks; create follow-up backlog items for immediate fixes.
Escalation contacts: PM (Maya Chen), Eng Lead (Arjun Patel), SRE on-call (rotation alias), Security (Lena Ruiz).
testing_plan:
- Contract tests: run for every PR touching API surface.
- Integration tests: streaming and structured outputs validated against harness.
- Performance tests: synthetic traffic to simulate 100 RPS for generation and 500 RPS for embeddings in pre-prod cluster sized to reflect warm production.
- Quality tests: nightly eval suite using curated prompts for chat/generation; embeddings similarity benchmark; rerank NDCG/precision tests.
- Chaos tests: network partition simulation across regions to validate fallback routing.
- Accessibility/Docs validation: sample quickstarts executed in CI for both Node and Python SDKs.
- Security/pen-test: CI run of static analysis; security team to perform focused review on auth/audit flows before GA.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards (Console pre-populated): token-cost per-route, latency heatmap by model variant, flow-level error rates, streaming drop-off rate, embedding batch latency distribution.
Primary alerts: 1) Routing surge / queue-depth > threshold, 2) p95 latency breach (endpoint-specific thresholds), 3) 5xx spike > 0.5% sustained 5m, 4) Billing event failure rate > 1% per minute.
SLOs: define per-endpoint p95 and error rate objectives and wire into SLO burn-down UIs.
Runbooks: short form automation for alert triage with runbook links embedded in alert messages.
Logging: sample request IDs preserved for 72h, with tracing hooks for cross-service span correlation.
Telemetry: export to metrics backend and sample logs to centralized retention for 30 days for GA customers (configurable for enterprise).
notes:
- Keep the API surface additive for v1.x; any breaking change requires migration guide and deprecation window of 90 days.
- Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to offer early access keys for top 10 customers during canary.
- Keep cost-optimization recommendations surfaced prominently in console to reduce sticker shock for embedding-heavy workloads.
- Document known limitations: rerank scaling with candidate count and truncation policy for embeddings > max tokens.
